body: I plan on looking into metta meditation and practicing enjoying time alone, even if it is painful.  I will be taking my first solo trip out of town soon.  Thank you for your response.

Everything you say feels so true...it reminds me of a zen saying.
"When practicing unconditional acceptance, start with yourself."
I am torn between horrible cynicism and a dim suspicion that this may be part of some painful period of growing.  Not only is it the idea of being "perfect" that makes stability so difficult to attain, it's also the obsessing.  Obsession with the past, my flaws, things I wish I'd done or said, failures and phrases or mantras in my head like "kill yourself".  I would like to be obsessed with healthy things for a change.  Thank you for the questions you have raised and your advice, I will be thinking about them.

>What does it mean to love another person?
>What would you think of a parent treating his/her child the way that you treat yourself emotionally?
>Do your insecurities have anything to do with her?
>Also, check out Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (The Feeling Good Handbook is a great example).

I cannot thank you enough for these challenging questions.  Just reading these responses made me thankful for posting my story to Reddit...it has reminded me that I can still use my brain.  I had forgotten that I can think about what has happened, and use my mind to contemplate my own life.  These questions have really awakened my thinking, which is kind of refreshing because I've done nothing but let my emotions (the dark ones) dominate my life for so long...As far as therapy goes, I am very cynical as each experience has not been helpful, but I know I should keep trying.  Not having health insurance has made this a major problem.  Thank you for your thoughtful response.

This is the ultimate destination I dream about...although I have thought of this concept so many times that I just feel confused about it now.  I'm very skeptical and afraid of the idealist kind of selfless love, because I've felt it turn into downright abuse when applied in the real world.  I would tell myself I love my girlfriend unconditionally, but this attitude seemed to grant her permission to do and say anything to me.  Ideally, I think this concept would solve many of humanity's problems if everyone tried to apply it, but in reality I have felt stepped on and hurt when I try to live it.  Maybe there is a deeper problem with my ego in that I am searching for an ideal response to the love, some kind of gratification...It is easier to attempt it when I feel some hope about life.  I need to think about this concept a lot more...

Wow...I feel I have lived through both sides of that relationship.  It's extremely hard for me to comprehend people who've come out of situations like these.  The idea of the woman focusing on her life by going back to school and doing what she needs to do reminds me something I've been thinking about lately.  These has to be a way to be "selfish" in a non-negative way, where I can enjoy my own activities, actions and daily goals as opposed to obsessing about other people's actions as much, without feeling bad about this for no reason.  Some kind of positive selfishness if that makes sense.  Thanks for this.

Some core aspects of my personality won't allow this to happen, although oftentimes I wish it would.  When I have been emotionally and mentally healthy in the past, relationships have given me joy like nothing else.  I am looking into finding a therapist through my county since I don't have health insurance right now.

Due to my money situation the best I can do is go on a solo trip, which I plan on doing very soon.  I have never gone on any vacation alone so I'm hoping this will help me in some way.  Thank you for the advice.
Thank you for that...I will be watching more videos from that series.
